lines.text: A coding agent is a model that uses tools in a loop.
It isn't autocomplete, and it isn't a chatbot.
It reads files, runs commands and edits code,|from a terminal, an editor, a desktop app or the web.
It picks which tools to use from your prompt,|and from what it learns along the way.
Give it a task, and it works in three phases.
It gathers context, takes action, then verifies the result,|and goes round again until the task is done.
You can step in at any point.|Press Escape to stop it, or type a correction and it adjusts.
lines.say: You can step in at any point. Press escape to stop it, or type a correction, and it adjusts.

lines.text: Risky actions are checked before they run:|in manual mode it asks you, in auto mode a classifier blocks them.
Before you type a word, its context window is already filling.
System instructions. Your CLAUDE.md. Saved memory.|A short description of every skill. The names of your MCP tools.
lines.say: System instructions. Your Claude dot M D. Saved memory. A short description of every skill. The names of your M C P tools.

lines.text: Then your prompt, and everything it reads and runs after that.
When the window gets full, old tool output is cleared first,|then the conversation is summarized.
So context is a budget, and every layer in this series spends some of it.|Slash context shows what loaded, and what each part costs.
Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Copilot run the same loop,|with their own names for the parts.
lines.say: Codex, Cursor, Gemini C L I and Copilot run the same loop, with their own names for the parts.

lines.text: Everyone rents the same models.|The setup around them is the part you build.
